title: Australia's defence alliance with Fiji comes into force
excerpt: A treaty committing Australia and Fiji to treat an armed attack on one as an attack on both has taken effect, with backing from both major parties.
content_html:
Australia's alliance with Fiji has formally taken effect, making the Pacific nation the fourth country with which Australia has a mutual defence commitment.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese told parliament on Thursday that the agreement was "a very important advance for both of our nations". It joins Australia's alliances with the United States, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea.

What the treaty says

The pact, signed in July, commits both countries to regard an armed attack on either one as an attack on both, AAP reported. Defence officials told a parliamentary inquiry in October that the wording was deliberately broad, so it would not automatically require a military response.

A linked agreement, known as the Vuvale Union, covers economic ties as well as co-operation on health, infrastructure, education and transnational crime. It also records both sides' view that military bases and visits by countries outside the arrangement could threaten security in the Pacific. AAP said it is the first agreement of its kind that Fiji has joined.

Fiji's High Commissioner to Australia, Ajay Amrit, and Fijian minister Ratu Antonio Lalabalavu watched from the gallery during Question Time.

Bipartisan support

Opposition Leader Angus Taylor backed the agreement in the chamber. "I join with the prime minister in that welcome and congratulations," he said.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong also described it as Australia's fourth formal alliance, NCA NewsWire reported.

A busy week in the Pacific

The Fiji pact came into force in the same week Albanese and Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale signed a separate treaty in Canberra on Wednesday. Under that deal, the Solomon Islands will not host a foreign military or security base, and Australia is recognised as its main security partner. Australia will also support the country's police force, border management, budget and education policy.

The Solomon Islands signed a security pact with China in 2022. Wale has said that agreement is under review, and that a confidentiality clause prevents him from discussing it.

The parties are divided over a third agreement, with Vanuatu. A parliamentary committee this week recommended ratifying the Nakamal Agreement, which includes commitments on net zero emissions by 2050. The Coalition says it will not support it unless the references to net zero and renewable energy targets are removed.

Defence Minister Richard Marles accused the Coalition of letting climate politics get in the way of a security agreement in the region.

editor_notes: Fiji alliance in force and fourth alliance: AAP (26 Nov) and NCA NewsWire (27 Nov, Wong). Mutual defence wording, July signing, October inquiry evidence, Vuvale Union content and bases language: AAP, attributed. Exact in-force date not available, so none given. Solomon Islands treaty (signed 25 Nov) used as context only: Defence Post plus NCA NewsWire mention; Yahoo/Defence Post conflict on whether China pact was ditched, so story uses Wale's own 'under review' position. Vanuatu: Coalition position stated alongside Marles's criticism for balance; Marles paraphrased. Two quotes (Albanese, Taylor), under 20 words, attributed.
